title: Protocol to locally express cxcl12a during zebrafish olfactory organ development by combining IR-LEGO with live imaging
protocol: Couple the IR-LEGO module to the infinity optical corrected input of the inverted microscope.
Use a spinning disk microscope dedicated to confocal fluorescence imaging in the visible range, coupled to an infrared photo-irradiation device.
Connect any microscope directly to its corrected optical input without intermediate lenses.
CallCheck in vivo IR irradiation condition using a dedicated tool (Calibration sample: Phosphor Micro Upconverting Particles) at the end of installation, to ensure hardware operability.
Prepare the desired fish lines for IR-LEGO and live imaging.
Obtain embryos through natural crosses.
Stage embryos according to established protocols.
Process the next morning.
Gently place female breeders on one side and male zebrafish on the other in a breeding tank divided by a temporary divider.
Remove the divider between breeders after the light is switched on in the morning to allow males and females to breed.
Remove the divider between males and females around 10 am.
Collect embryos using an egg strainer 30 minutes after removing the divider.
Transfer collected embryos into a Petri dish filled with fish water.
Place embryos in a 28.5°C incubator to grow to 11 hpf for IR-LEGO and time-lapse imaging.
Regularly remove dead embryos and unfertilized eggs.
Change fish water regularly (at least twice a day) until the embryos are processed.
Sort the proper staged embryos for fluorescent expression under a stereo zoom microscope (SMZ18 Nikon).
Transfer selected embryos to a Petri dish with fish water.
Remove the chorion under a stereoscopic microscope equipped with a transmitted light source.
Gently make a tear in the chorion using dissecting tweezers.
Turn the embryo upside down so that it falls out of the chorion.
Prepare 0.7% low melting (LM) agarose mounting solution, mixing sterile fish water and LM agarose to form a homogeneous solution.
Microwave the solution until the LM has completely dissolved in the fish water.
Place dissolved LM agarose in a pre-equilibrated 32°C water bath to cool for about 20 min.
Add 120 μL of 0.7% LM agarose in fish water heated at 32°C into one glass Petri dish.
Transfer the dechorionated embryos to the agarose drop using a glass Pasteur pipet.
Place the embryos in the orientation with the black arrowhead pointing towards the anterior part, the head, of the embryo.
Place the 2 mL tube containing the 0.7% LM agarose solution in a dry bath at 90°C for 15 min to melt the agarose.
Transfer the tube from the 90°C dry bath to a dry bath set at 32°C and maintain it there for up to 45 min.
Use a traceable thermometer to monitor the temperature of the melted agarose, ensuring it does not exceed 35°C.
Discard any remaining agarose that has not been completely used after melting.
Transfer the embryos using a fine tip glass Pasteur pipet.
Position the embryos dorsally using dissecting forceps before the 0.7% LM agarose solidifies.
Mount the embryos with somites and trunks at the top, and the olfactory system near the glass slide for observation.
Wait for the agarose to solidify after positioning all embryos.
Fill the glass Petri dish with 1 mL of 0.7% low melting agarose to stabilize the mounting device.
Cover the embryos in the agarose with 2 mL of sterile fish water.
Annotate the position of each embryo on the lid of the glass Petri dish.
Set up the noise to signal conditions before using the IR-LEGO
Power on the Leica Spinning Disk confocal microscope.
Open Metamorph software.
Open SysCon software from Rapp OptoElectronic GmbH.
Load the correct journal in Metamorph to connect with SysCon.
Select the APO 40×/1.3 oil objective.
Place the 35 mm Petri dish containing the mounted embryos on the microscope stage.
Use white light to localize the anterior brain of the first embryo.
Set the Z stack range around the current position on Metamorph.
Mark the position for multiposition setup.
Repeat steps for every embryo.
Set the wavelength parameters in green channel for Tg(cldnb:lyn-GFP) visualization using 488 nm excitation and a band emission filter of 510-540 nm.
Use low laser power (∼2% of 150 mW laser).
Apply short exposure time (50 ms) to minimize photobleaching.
Set the wavelength parameters in red channel for Tg(hsp:mcherry-cxcl12a) visualization using 561 nm excitation.
Use minimal laser power and exposure time to minimize phototoxicity when acquiring images.
Acquire a stack at both wavelengths with 143 planes every 0.7 μm using automated stages for multiple position acquisition.
Control the timing and pattern of activation of your gene of interest (mcherry-cxcl12a) using IR-LEGO.
Open the IR light path input on the Leica microscope control stand and select the right cube, D1.
Check the setup to ensure correct reflection of the IR laser onto the sample and imaging using the spinning disk.
Turn on the IR laser and open SysCon software to pilot it.
Select the IR-APO 40×/1.10 W CORR objective adapted for IR irradiation.
Choose the embryo you want to irradiate within Metamorph’s “Multiposition” folder.
Manually select the z plane of your choice in the telencephalon center using claudin-GFP live imaging.
Select the Infrared laser (light source DL-1470/2500/RSP2) in SysCon software.
Load the last Laser calibration folder.
Click on “center spot” to place the laser in the middle of the field.
Choose the ROI corresponding to this laser spot position using the sequence manager in SysCon software.
Set the IR laser intensity to 90% in the system.
Open the IR shutter and click on the “OFF” Status button to activate (ON) the IR laser for 1 min.
Close the IR shutter and click on the “ON” Status button to inactivate (OFF) the IR laser.
Repeat steps for each embryo to be irradiated.
Close SysCon software.
Close the IR light path input on the microscope (manual shutter).
Switch off the IR laser.
Launch the 24 h acquisition.
Remove your sample and shut down the system at the end of the time-lapse acquisition.
